claim: Awake hippocampal replay is not just memory playback: it runs forward before movement and in reverse after arrival, with direction tied to timing (Diba and Buzsaki: 95% of significant forward events before the run, 85% of reverse after).
agent_test: Add a post-outcome backward walk (outcome to earlier steps) versus forward-only review; same token cap; compare error-localisation accuracy.
audit_note: Foster and Wilson 2006 and Diba and Buzsaki 2007 abstracts confirm reverse replay after the run and forward sequences before it; the 95%/85% figures are stated in the Diba figure legend, which I could only reach through a search-result summary because the PMC and Nature pages blocked direct fetch.

claim: Reverse replay rate (not forward) tracks reward change, consistent with a credit-assignment role.
agent_test: Vary reward feedback size; test whether a backward-chain revision step beats forward re-read only when feedback changes.

claim: Pre-choice replay encodes the future path to a remembered goal, including paths to non-home goals (Pfeiffer and Foster 2013: 2,028 trajectory events, 0 with P>0.02; away-events matched future path, P 4.96e-22).
agent_test: Compare rollout of candidate plans before acting against act-then-revise at equal tokens.

claim: Replay content before choice reflects reliably rewarded and less recently visited places, not the upcoming choice (Gillespie 2021: eight-arm win-stay lose-switch, 4 rats), challenging the plan reading of Pfeiffer and Foster. Reconciled in part: the same rats switch mode with engagement (Olafsdottir 2017, 8 rats: 62.26% direction-congruent when engaged vs 52.19% when disengaged) and humans show on-task replay with replanning but off-task replay of preferred paths (Eldar 2020, N=40).
agent_test: Test whether a memory-maintenance pass (revisit rewarded, stale items) helps over a plan-the-next-step pass.

claim: Preplay of novel-track sequences exists in the Dragoi lab data: 14.2% of events significant (P<1e-32, 3 mice), 9.8% in rats, 82.6% track coverage, capacity estimate about 15 tracks. Naive rat pups show preplay-like sequences from P17-18 (Farooq and Dragoi 2019), but that is the same lab.
agent_test: Not directly testable; used only as prior on pre-built structure.

claim: Silva, Feng and Foster 2015 failed to find preplay: median abs correlation 0.174 real vs 0.172 shuffle (p=0.08) in 9,803 Sleep-1 events; 435/442 units well clustered; NMDA blockade (D-CPPene) before Runs 2 and 3 prevented trajectory events. Verified in full text this session.
agent_test: Interpretation: thresholds and templates drive preplay claims. For the agent, do not credit pre-planned structure without a shuffled-control comparison.

claim: Preplay-like sequences can be produced by random clustered networks (Breffle 2024; capacity about 8.6 vs about 15 tracks), so preplay does not prove a dedicated forecasting mechanism.
agent_test: Use as caution when claiming the agent needs special 'preconfigured' scaffolds; test random structure versus designed structure.

claim: Preplay to goals is conditional: cued arm 7.37% (p<0.001) vs uncued 4.41% (p=0.33), 4 rats, so motivational relevance and visual access gate it (Olafsdottir 2015).
agent_test: Check whether stating the goal first raises rollout quality for goal-relevant branches only.

claim: Most sharp-wave ripple events carry spatially coherent content (Denovellis 2021: 96% of 23,071 classified SWRs coherent, 14% had any incoherent segment, 10 rats), and many progress at roughly real-world movement speed rather than the roughly 20x compressed speed reported in earlier work; how much replay is detected depends on the decoding assumptions, while fast compressed replay is still documented on long tracks (Davidson 2009, about 8 m/s virtual speed).
agent_test: Decoder choice changes conclusions; require the agent's replay-evaluation to use more than one scoring rule.
audit_note: Denovellis 2021 confirms 96% (22,170 of 23,071) coherent, 14% (3,295 of 23,071) with any incoherent segment, 10 rats. But the paper says events often progress slower than previously reported (~20x compressed) and closer to real-world (wake) speed, not 'slower than real time'; and it attributes the lower prevalence in older work to differing decoding assumptions (linear fits), not a decoder 'artefact'; Davidson 2009 documents fast (~8 m/s virtual) replay on long tracks.
claim_before_audit: Most sharp-wave ripple replay is spatially coherent and often slower than real time (Denovellis 2021: 96% of 23,071 classified SWRs coherent, 14% had any incoherent segment, 10 rats); older fast-replay accounts are partly a decoder artefact.

claim: Replay length extends beyond one ripple by chaining (Davidson 2009: 19% of events over 250 ms; durations 40-1018 ms, 4 rats).
agent_test: Test chained rollouts of fixed total tokens versus several short ones.

claim: Replay of remote experience happens in a new context and declines after long stillness (Karlsson and Frank: 47% of 612 events in first exposure; 34.2% after >60 s immobility).
agent_test: Test whether recalling an earlier problem during a new problem improves it at equal tokens.

claim: A recurrent network trained for planning that learns to do imagined rollouts reproduces rat replay effects (Jensen 2024: home-trial success 0.622 true goal vs 0.403 disjoint control; human think-time correlation r=0.186, falling to 0.070 after distance control).
agent_test: Count rollouts vs accuracy on small search tasks; check diminishing returns after about 15 rollouts.

claim: Reward-driven replay emerges without design in RL agents and in a prioritisation model; cheaper rules perform close to full prioritisation (Diekmann 2023).
agent_test: Compare random replay to value-prioritised replay in memory review at equal tokens. Evidence is qualitative in c05.

claim: Pre-computing over a known context before queries arrive cuts test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy and adds up to +13% (GSM-Symbolic) and +18% (AIME); 2.5x cost drop at 10 queries per context; 5 parallel generations beat 10. Full text verified this session. Authors state the gain shrinks when queries are hard to predict; the accuracy gap widens across predictability bins; no zero-gain point was measured.
agent_test: Run idle-time precompute on the agent's own notes before the question; match total tokens including the precompute.

claim: Brain-inspired memory/replay LLM-agent systems report gains but none isolates a replay step (BrainMem EB-ALFRED GPT-4o 64.0 to 82.0 under full ablation ladder, 2-point steps). Under token matching, vanilla extra steps match or beat AWM, ASI and ReasoningBank (Gemini 3 Flash average 44.78 vs 39.34, 41.02, 39.33).
agent_test: Ablate replay alone from a memory stack at equal tokens, 5+ seeds, 100+ tasks.

claim: Experience-replay-style LLM agents gain from stored past trajectories (AWM +24.6% Mind2Web, +51.1% WebArena relative; Reflexion 91% vs 80% HumanEval; Voyager 3.3x items), but these are memory results, not tests of preplay.
agent_test: Ablate trajectory reuse versus fresh solve at equal tokens.
audit_note: arXiv abstracts confirm AWM +24.6% Mind2Web and +51.1% WebArena relative, Reflexion 91% vs 80% HumanEval (GPT-4 baseline), Voyager 3.3x unique items; ExpeL abstract has no numbers. 'Experience replay style' is the claim's own framing; the papers store workflows, reflections and skills, not raw trajectories, and none tests preplay.

claim: No LLM study directly tests preplay or replay recording paradigms; transformer-hippocampus links are formal (Whittington) with no replay measurement.
agent_test: Our own test is the first: operationalise forward rollout before act and backward revision after outcome as separate operators.
audit_note: Whittington 2022 abstract: formal link between transformers with recurrent position encodings and hippocampal models, no replay or preplay measurement; my arXiv and Semantic Scholar queries found no LLM preplay study. Absence claim, so only as strong as the searches.

claim: Hindsight relabelling (replaying failed trajectories with new goals) is an AI analogue of reverse/alternative replay but needs goal-conditioned setups.
agent_test: Test relabelling failed attempts as solutions to the sub-goal they did reach.

claim: Cognitive-map planning is weak in LLMs on CogEval (2023 models): GPT-4 scores 0.99 on 1-step paths, 0.47 on n-step paths, 0.21 on policy revaluation; shortest path one cluster away succeeded 0 of 30 at temperature 0.
agent_test: Re-run CogEval-style graph tasks with current models, with and without an explicit edge list to roll out over.

claim: Foster and Wilson 2006 supplies only a qualitative claim here (awake reverse replay right after a run, linked to reinforcement-learning-style evaluation). No counts or compression factors could be obtained from an open source; cite no figure from it.
agent_test: Use Diba and Buzsaki and Pfeiffer and Foster for figures; open the paper through a library before citing numbers.

claim: Awake replay switches between a plan-like mode near action points and a consolidate-like mode in long stillness: engaged 62.26% congruent and 80.70% local; disengaged 52.19% and 71.42% (both chance); engaged content predicts turn accuracy at 60.3% (p=0.02). 8 rats, 1,415 vs 3,010 events.
agent_test: Test a plan pass at decision points and a review pass during idle time, versus one mixed pass, at equal tokens.

claim: In humans, on-task replay tracks flexibility and replanning, while off-task replay tracks rehearsal of previously preferred paths (MEG, N=40; r=0.32 between post-outcome decodability and on-task sequenceness).
agent_test: Check whether an idle review pass that only re-reads preferred answers raises confident error.

claim: Prioritising replay by Need times Gain beats random-order replay in gridworld simulation; priority in LLM RL training needs an age decay (FreshPER +46% NQ Search, +367% Sokoban vs on-policy; plain PER degrades). No LLM memory-review test of prioritised vs random replay exists.
agent_test: Compare value-and-recency-ordered review against random review in a memory loop at equal tokens.

claim: Under matched tokens, extra acting steps match or beat memory modules (AWM, ASI, ReasoningBank) on WebArena across three models and on WorkArena-L1, so memory or replay gains must be shown against an equal-token retry arm.
agent_test: Always include an equal-token retry arm; report run-to-run spread over 3 or more seeds.

claim: Comparing several attempts at the same task and consolidating with explicit rules beats single-attempt summaries (WebArena 61.30, 70.10, then 72.90 with add-and-delete) while free rewriting hurts (54.57); plain accumulation eventually falls below no memory (Hippo, one paper, own harness; no-memory at-least-once over 8 attempts is 73.6%).
agent_test: Test cross-attempt comparison with rule-bound merge against append-only and free-rewrite stores, with a retry arm.

claim: Forward foresight tools are underused and sometimes harmful: some agents invoke simulation under 1% of the time, about 15% of rollouts are misused, up to 5% degradation (Qian 2026); WebATLAS look-ahead belongs to a 63.0 vs 53.9 result but is not isolated.
agent_test: Make rollout conditional on a trigger and check how its output is used; compare with act-then-revise at equal tokens.

claim: Backward credit assignment helps in training (HCAPO +13.8 ALFWorld, +7.7 WebShop over GRPO) but naming the culprit step is hard for frontier LLMs (best handcraft Who&When step-level accuracy 20.68%, Claude-Sonnet-4).
agent_test: Require evidence and a replay-with-fix check before accepting a blamed step; compare with forward re-read at equal tokens.

claim: Preplay-like pre-existing sequences were extended to developing rats (same lab) and to human temporal cortex (a looser test). No independent hippocampal preplay replication with 2023-2026 data was found beyond Silva 2015, Olafsdottir 2015 and Breffle 2024.
agent_test: Treat preplay as a prior, not a demonstrated planning mechanism.

claim: Multitask Preplay (counterfactual pre-solving of reachable but unpursued tasks) predicts human path reuse (about 62%, N=100 per experiment) and reaches about 97.5% success where goal relabelling gets 5.56-8.22%; tested only in grid worlds and Craftax.
agent_test: Test spare-compute pre-solving of nearby problem variants on language tasks at equal tokens.
